about: A command-line tool that lets a team share the skills and settings of their AI coding assistants from one place.

prs.title: Empty settings files no longer pile up in members' projects
prs.broken: When the team removed the last of its shared tool connections, each member's next update left empty settings files behind. No longer hidden from git, they showed up as new files and were easy to commit by mistake.
prs.changed: Updating now deletes a settings file it leaves empty, as the cleanup commands already did. Files with anything else in them, or that git tracks, stay.
prs.matters: Members' projects stay clean, with nothing stray to commit.

prs.title: Files the team deleted no longer come back
prs.broken: When someone deleted a file from a shared skill, every teammate's copy kept it. The next time a teammate shared their copy, the deleted file returned for everyone.
prs.changed: Updating now removes a file the team deleted, as long as the teammate never changed it. Files they added themselves stay.
prs.matters: Cleanups stick, and shared skills stop growing back old files.

prs.title: Moved coding sessions keep the edits they made
prs.broken: TeamAI can move a coding session from one AI tool to another. Every file edit made in Codex lost its content on the way, and the tool still said nothing was lost.
prs.changed: I made it read the edit's content from the place Codex keeps it.
prs.matters: A moved or archived session still shows what each edit changed.

prs.title: Moved coding sessions keep their turns in order
prs.broken: Moving a Claude Code session with the tool could scramble it: every question came first, then every answer. The tool still reported the move as fully faithful.
prs.changed: The tool now follows each conversation thread from start to end before the next one, so a session reads back in its real order.
prs.matters: A moved session reads like the conversation that really happened.

prs.title: Codex reasoning comes through when a session moves
prs.broken: Moving a Codex session to another tool lost all of Codex's reasoning. The tool looked for it in a place Codex never writes, so every reasoning step came out empty.
prs.changed: I made the tool read the reasoning from where Codex really keeps it, and still read the old place first so nothing else changes.
prs.matters: A moved Codex session keeps the model's thinking, not a row of blank blocks.

prs.title: Codex tool output keeps its text when sessions move
prs.broken: When a Codex session was moved or archived, tool results stored as a list came out as "[object Object]" instead of their text.
prs.changed: I made the reader join the text parts of such results, the same way it already does for Claude Code.
prs.matters: Moved sessions keep what the tools actually printed.
